extraction.name: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation
extraction.description: The generative capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly expanding from static code to dynamic, interactive visual artifacts. This progress is bottlenecked by a critical evaluation gap: established benchmarks focus on algorithmic correctness and largely overlook the visual fidelity and interactive integrity that define modem user experiences. To bridge this gap, we introduceArtifactsBench, a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation. Our framework renders each artifact and captures its dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots. This visual evidence, alongside the source code, is then assessed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge, which is rigorously guided by afine-grained, per-task checklistto ensure holistic and reproducible scoring. We curate1,825diverse tasks and evaluate over 30 leading LLMs. Our automated evaluation achieves 94.4%ranking consistency with WebDev Arena—a de facto gold standard for human preferences in web development—and up to90.95%pairwise agreement with human experts. We opensource ArtifactsBench, including the benchmark, evaluation hamess, and baseline results at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io , to provide the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team, Chenchen Zhang, Yuhang Li, Can Xu, Jiaheng Liu, Ao Liu, Changzhi Zhou, Ken Deng, Dengpeng Wu, Guanhua Huang, Kejiao Li, Qi Yi, Ruibin Xiong, Shihui Hu, Yue Zhang, Yuhao Jiang, Zenan Xu, Yuanxing Zhang, Wiggin Zhou, Chayse Zhou, Fengzong Lian
extraction.citeAs: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation by Tencent Hunyuan Team et al.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated via a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement. The pipeline ensures rich dynamics, real interactivity, clean and traceable provenance, strict de-duplication/contamination control, and reproducibility via standardized execution and checklist-guided judging. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Prompts were rewritten by experts and LLMs for clarity, completeness, and executability, then verified by humans. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs. Solvability validation and ambiguity repair involved collecting candidate solutions from multiple families and pruning underspecified items, revising or removing tasks solved only by brittle hacks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Surveys, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were rewritten by experts for clarity, completeness, and executability, with LLM rewriting adding diverse styles, and human verification. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed to ensure answerability and unambiguousness.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters were used to drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics. A two-stage de-duplication and contamination control process involved MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, and screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were initially LLM-drafted (by Hunyuan-Turbos) and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and was reused as few-shot references to maintain high difficulty and consistent rubrics. Each dimension is scored on 10-point scales with detailed rubrics, penalizing redundancy and rewarding innovation, with code-level checks revealing issues beyond visual inspection. The 10 items are grouped into five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: MLLM-as-Judge (Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen2.5-VL-72B) for automated scoring. Human annotators (front-end engineers) for validation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A 10% manually curated seed achieved Cohen’s κ≥0.8 among annotators. A double-blind human evaluation study on 280 queries and 6 models, judged by multiple front-end engineers, measured agreement by Pair ACC. Pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) was computed between MLLM referee and human judges.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Dual-referee setup (Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B) for automated scoring. For human validation, multiple engineers independently scored selected queries.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior by capturing and analyzing a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. The benchmark currently focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn from a given prompt, and does not assess an LLM’s capability to function as an autonomous agent that can iteratively refine an artifact based on feedback, debug its own code, or plan and execute a multi-step development process.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation, Testing, Validation of Large Language Models (LLMs) on their ability to generate dynamic, interactive visual artifacts. The benchmark provides a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models.
